- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 3–7% if recent history shows sustained upward trend.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day spikes; smooth out forecast peaks by reducing amplitude by 10–15%.
- Apply mean reversion bias correction: if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15%.
- Lag correction: if forecast is significantly ahead of true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), delay peak by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high volatility; dampen forecast sensitivity to short-term noise by applying a 30-day moving average filter.
